elements_zh.main_results: 与体重正常的儿童相比,肥胖儿童的结合抗体数量更高,但中和抗体无差异。瘦素与更高的结合抗体数量相关,而脂联素与更低的结合抗体数量相关,两者均未影响中和抗体水平。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,肥胖与初次感染后DENV结合抗体数量增加有关,但与中和抗体质量无关,暗示肥胖儿童的抗体中和效率较低。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果表明,瘦素和脂联素等脂联素类物质可用于补充BMIz分析或作为独立的免疫应答预测因子,强调了在理解登革病毒(DENV)感染中考虑脂肪标志物的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括其观察性质以及可能存在的混杂因素,这可能影响证据的强度。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the association between obesity and antibody responses to dengue virus in children, addressing the gap in understanding how nutritional status influences immune responses to dengue infection.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated 85 children from the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary dengue virus infection in 2019, assessing the impact of body mass index z-score, leptin, and adiponectin on binding and neutralizing antibody responses.
analysis_en.methods: Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and dengue infection outcome, with binding and neutralizing antibody responses measured using specific assays.
analysis_en.main_results: Children with obesity had higher quantities of binding antibodies but no difference in neutralizing antibodies compared to those with normal weight. Leptin was associated with higher binding antibodies, while adiponectin was associated with lower binding antibodies, with no effect on neutralizing antibodies.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) post-primary dengue infection, implying lower neutralization efficiency in children with obesity.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results indicate that adipokines, such as leptin and adiponectin, are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses, highlighting the importance of considering body fat markers in understanding immune responses to dengue virus.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the observational nature and the potential for confounding factors, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 儿童肥胖与初次感染后登革病毒(DENV)结合抗体反应增加有关,但与中和抗体反应无关
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Obesity has been associated with higher risk of dengue virus (DENV) infection and disease, yet its influence on antibody responses to DENV remains undefined. Methods We evaluated whether nutritional status—based on body mass index z-score (BMIz)—or blood markers of body fat—leptin and adiponectin—are associated with binding and/or neutralizing antibody responses to DENV in 85 children in the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study who experienced a primary DENV infection in 2019. Associations were estimated using linear models adjusting for age, sex, and DENV infection outcome. Results Compared with children with normal weight, those with obesity had higher quantities of DENV binding antibodies (fold-change [FC] 1.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02, 3.48) but no difference in neutralizing antibodies. Likewise, leptin concentration was associated with higher quantities of binding antibodies (FC 1.22, 95% CI 1.09, 1.37), while adiponectin was associated with lower quantities (FC 0.79, 95% CI .67, .94), and neither was associated with neutralizing antibodies. Lower neutralizing efficiency (neutralizing/binding antibodies) was observed in children with obesity (FC 0.67, 95% CI .48, .93). Conclusions Our results indicate that obesity is associated with higher antibody quantity (binding) but not higher quality (neutralization) postprimary DENV infection—implying that antibodies generated by children with obesity have lower neutralization efficiency, requiring greater quantities to reach similar levels of neutralization than children with normal weight. Further, the agreement among the 3 models using distinct proxies of body fat—BMIz, leptin, and adiponectin—demonstrates that adipokines are useful in supplementing BMIz analysis or as independent predictors of immune responses.

papers.title: Presence of Heterozygous V1016G kdr Mutation in Pyrethroid Insecticide Resistance in Aedes aegypti a Dengue vector from Southern India.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of Dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its control relies heavily on pyrethroid insecticides. However, the development of resistance in mosquito populations poses a major challenge to effective vector control. This study aimed to investigate the presence of the V1016G knockdown resistance (kdr) mutation in Aedes aegypti collected from Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, India. METHODS: Aedes immatures were collected from selected field sites and subjected to insecticide susceptibility testing using World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines. Genomic DNA was extracted, and allele-specific PCR was performed to detect the V1016G mutation in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene (vgsc). RESULTS: The analysis revealed the presence of the V1016G mutation in heterozygous form (VG) among the tested samples. No homozygous mutants (GG) were detected. The presence of heterozygous individuals indicates an early stage of resistance development, likely due to ongoing insecticide selection pressure. Bioassay results showed reduced susceptibility to pyrethroids in these populations, supporting the molecular findings. CONCLUSION: This study provides baseline data on the genetic mechanism of pyrethroid resistance in Aedes aegypti from Nagapattinam district. Regular monitoring of kdr mutations is essential to detect resistance early and guide insecticide use policies. Integrating molecular surveillance with conventional control measures will help delay the spread of resistance and improve the long-term success of vector management programs. The findings highlight the need for alternative control strategies and responsible insecticide use to maintain the effectiveness of current interventions.

papers.title: Synergistic Effects of pH and Temperature on Dengue Virus Envelope Dimers: Insights from Microsecond Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Dengue pathogenesis depends on a conformational rearrangement of the envelope glycoprotein (pE) induced by low pH. However, how pH and temperature cooperate to destabilize the dimeric form of the pE, a fundamental step that enables the formation of the fusion-active trimer, remains unclear. Here, we investigate this synergy for Dengue serotypes of greatest medical relevance, DENV-2 and DENV-3. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations were performed on the microsecond scale, at 28 °C, 37 °C, and 40 °C under pH 5, 6, and 7 using CHARMM36m force fields and complemented by extended coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations for the DENV-2 system at 37 °C and pH 5, and for the DENV-3 system at 28 °C and pH 5, and at 37 °C and pH 7. Our simulations suggest that increasing the temperature from 28 to 37 °C tends to expand the conformational space at neutral pH, potentially weakening dimer integrity through modulation of the interfacial interaction network. Acidification appears to amplify this effect in a serotype-specific manner: in our simulations DENV-2 required pH 5, while DENV-3 responded at pH 6. Additionally, distance and principal component analyses revealed an asymmetric dissociation pathway, termed the "compensatory embrace", observed in both all-atom and coarse-grained models. Structural analyses further highlighted the differences in histidine distribution between the serotypes. Moreover, interaction mapping at 37 °C identified candidate interfacial contacts that may act as pH-sensitive latches, maintaining stability at pH 7 but breaking upon acidification. Collectively, these results suggest a potential hierarchy of physicochemical triggers that may contribute to the conversion of dimer into fusion-competent monomers. These interfacial hotspots and the "compensatory embrace" constitute structurally informed targets that, pending validation under native virion conditions, may guide the rational design of antivirals and immunogens, underscoring the value of long-time scale molecular dynamics simulations as a hypothesis-generating tool in drug discovery.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨pH和温度对登革病毒DENV-2和DENV-3包膜糖蛋白(pE)二聚体形式的协同效应,这对于形成融合活性三聚体至关重要。登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的pE构象重排,但pH和温度如何协同作用的机制仍不清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用CHARMM36m力场,在不同温度(28 °C、37 °C、40 °C)和pH值(5、6、7)条件下,对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了微秒级的分子动力学模拟。此外,还在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。
elements_zh.methods: 进行了微秒级的全原子分子动力学模拟,并在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。模拟使用CHARMM36m力场进行。
elements_zh.main_results: 模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱"。结构分析突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异,相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果总体上表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,可用于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解登革病毒和发病机制的分子机制提供了见解,并可能指导抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了分子动力学模拟,这些是计算模型,可能无法完全捕捉病毒的所有行为。研究结果仅适用于所测试的条件,可能无法推广到所有生理条件。模拟是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全代表原生病毒颗粒环境的复杂性。

papers.abstract_zh: 登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的包膜糖蛋白(pE)构象重排。然而,pH和温度如何协同作用以破坏pE的二聚体形式,这是形成融合活性三聚体的基本步骤,目前仍不清楚。在此,我们研究了对登革热最具医学意义的DENV-2和DENV-3血清型中pH和温度的协同效应。使用CHARMM36m力场,在28 °C、37 °C和40 °C温度下,pH 5、6和7条件下进行了全原子分子动力学模拟。此外,对于DENV-2系统,在37 °C和pH 5条件下,以及DENV-3系统在28 °C和pH 5条件下,以及37 °C和pH 7条件下,还进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。我们的模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能通过调节界面相互作用网络而削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化似乎以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应:在我们的模拟中,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱",在全原子和粗粒度模型中均观察到。结构分析进一步突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异。此外,在37 °C条件下进行的相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁,维持pH 7时的稳定性,但在酸化条件下会断裂。总体而言,这些结果表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,待在原生病毒颗粒条件下验证后,可能有助于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨pH和温度对登革病毒DENV-2和DENV-3包膜糖蛋白(pE)二聚体形式的协同效应,这对于形成融合活性三聚体至关重要。登革病毒发病机制依赖于由低pH诱导的pE构象重排,但pH和温度如何协同作用的机制仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用CHARMM36m力场,在不同温度(28 °C、37 °C、40 °C)和pH值(5、6、7)条件下,对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了微秒级的分子动力学模拟。此外,还在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行了微秒级的全原子分子动力学模拟,并在特定条件下对DENV-2和DENV-3进行了扩展的粗粒度分子动力学模拟。模拟使用CHARMM36m力场进行。
analysis_zh.main_results: 模拟结果表明,温度从28 °C升高到37 °C会扩大中性pH下的构象空间,可能削弱二聚体的完整性。酸化以血清型特异性方式放大了这一效应,DENV-2需要pH 5,而DENV-3则在pH 6时产生反应。距离和主成分分析揭示了一条不对称的解离路径,称为"补偿性拥抱"。结构分析突出了不同血清型之间组氨酸分布的差异,相互作用图谱识别了候选的界面接触点,这些接触点可能作为pH敏感的闩锁。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些结果总体上表明可能存在一种物理化学触发因素的层次结构,这可能有助于二聚体向融合活性单体的转化。这些界面热点和"补偿性拥抱"构成了结构信息指导的目标,可用于抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为理解登革病毒和发病机制的分子机制提供了见解,并可能指导抗病毒药物和免疫原的合理设计,强调了在药物发现中长时尺度分子动力学模拟作为假设生成工具的价值。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于使用了分子动力学模拟,这些是计算模型,可能无法完全捕捉病毒的所有行为。研究结果仅适用于所测试的条件,可能无法推广到所有生理条件。模拟是在受控条件下进行的,可能无法完全代表原生病毒颗粒环境的复杂性。

papers.title_original: Questioning the role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study questions the role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue, as it is widely thought to explain the disease's severity, while acknowledging that other pathobiological steps may also contribute.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature and does not involve a specific study design or population, focusing instead on the broader scientific context of dengue disease and its pathogenesis.
analysis.methods: The methods involve a comprehensive review of published research on dengue virus infection, including references to multiple studies and their findings on antibody-dependent enhancement and other factors contributing to severe dengue.
analysis.main_results: The study highlights that antibody-dependent enhancement is not the sole or primary mechanism responsible for severe dengue, and that multiple interdependent pathobiological steps may play a role in the development of life-threatening disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue is questionable and suggest that other factors may be more significant, offering a novel perspective on the pathogenesis of dengue disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform future research on dengue pathogenesis and could influence the development of more effective diagnostic tools, treatments, and vaccines by shifting focus from antibody-dependent enhancement to other contributing mechanisms.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing literature and does not present original data, which may affect the strength of its conclusions. However, it provides a critical analysis of current understanding and highlights gaps in evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study questions the widely accepted role of antibody-dependent enhancement in severe dengue, suggesting that multiple interdependent pathobiological steps may contribute to the disease's severity. The authors review existing literature to argue that the focus on antibody-dependent enhancement may be misplaced, and that other factors are more significant in the development of life-threatening dengue. The findings may inform future research and influence the development of diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive strategies for dengue. However, the study is limited to a literature review and does not present original data, which may affect the strength of its conclusions. The evidence is considered moderate due to its reliance on secondary sources and the absence of direct experimental findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究质疑抗体依赖性增强在重症登革热中的作用,因为其被广泛认为可以解释疾病的严重程度,同时承认其他病原生物学步骤也可能有所贡献。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对现有文献的综述,不涉及特定的研究设计或人群,而是更关注登革病及其发病机制的更广泛科学背景。
elements_zh.methods: 该方法涉及对登革病毒感染相关已发表研究的全面回顾,包括多个研究及其关于抗体依赖性增强和其他因素对重症登革热影响的发现。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究指出,抗体依赖性增强并不是重症登革热的唯一或主要机制,多个相互依赖的病原生物学步骤可能在潜在致命性疾病的发展中发挥作用。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为抗体依赖性增强在重症登革热中的作用值得质疑,并提出其他因素可能更为重要,为登革病的发病机制提供了新的视角。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能有助于未来关于登革病发病机制的研究,并可能影响更有效的诊断工具、治疗和疫苗的开发,通过将研究重点从抗体依赖性增强转移到其他贡献机制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于现有文献的回顾,未提供原始数据,这可能影响其结论的强度。然而,它对当前理解进行了批判性分析,并指出了证据中的空白。

papers.title: Structure-Guided Design of a Subnanomolar Dengue Virus NS4B Inhibitor.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus nonstructural protein 4B (NS4B) is an essential regulator of viral replication but remains structurally unresolved, limiting drug discovery. Here, we combine modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to enable structure-guided inhibition of NS4B. Comparative models across all four serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket consistent with resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that guide the development of predictive field-based 3D-QSAR models (R = 0.91, Q = 0.89). Prospective screening of bioisosteric and in-house compounds identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity across all four dengue serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 (IC50 = 0.17 nM) with a high selectivity index (∼37,000). Conserved binding interactions across serotypes support broad-spectrum potential. This study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of structurally unresolved dengue virus NS4B, which limits drug discovery. The research combines modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to guide the development of structure-based inhibitors. Comparative models across all four dengue serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket, suggesting resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that support the creation of predictive 3D-QSAR models. Prospective screening identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity against all four serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 with a high selectivity index. Conserved binding interactions across serotypes suggest broad-spectrum potential, supporting the development of new therapeutic strategies. The study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.

papers.title_zh: 基于结构设计的亚纳摩尔级 登革病毒 NS4B 抑制剂
papers.source_body_en: Dengue virus nonstructural protein 4B (NS4B) is an essential regulator of viral replication but remains structurally unresolved, limiting drug discovery. Here, we combine modeling, ligand-based design, and experimental validation to enable structure-guided inhibition of NS4B. Comparative models across all four serotypes reveal a conserved transmembrane binding pocket consistent with resistance mutations. Docking of JNJ-series inhibitors defines key interaction features that guide the development of predictive field-based 3D-QSAR models (R = 0.91, Q = 0.89). Prospective screening of bioisosteric and in-house compounds identifies BNJ-495 as a candidate broad-spectrum inhibitor with predicted activity across all four dengue serotypes. Experimental validation confirms potent activity against dengue virus serotype 2 (IC50 = 0.17 nM) with a high selectivity index (∼37,000). Conserved binding interactions across serotypes support broad-spectrum potential. This study establishes a general framework for targeting structurally elusive viral membrane proteins.

papers.title: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels
papers.abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

papers.title_zh: 温带地区登革热病例增加与巴西Aedes aegypti入侵和滋生水平相关
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热(登革热),由登革病毒(登革病毒,DENV)引起,是全球最严重的蚊媒传染病之一,其风险因Aedes aegypti(媒介)向亚热带和温带地区的扩展而增加。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024年,巴西占全球报告登革热病例的70%,并且该病毒最近已在巴西最南端的里约格兰德 do 硫磺州(Rio Grande do Sul)成为地方性流行病。
analysis_zh.methods: 在此研究中,我们整合了生态学、流行病学和环境数据,并生成了互补的基因组数据,以研究2015年至2023年间巴西南部地区的登革病毒动态。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在此期间,Aedes aegypti在州内各市镇广泛扩散,自2020年起登革热病例显著增加。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 对665例新登革病毒(基因组)的基因组分析与病毒株在多年内的本地持续存在一致,驱动了季节性暴发的传播。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现突显了登革热向温带地区从北向南扩展的趋势,强调了在新出现的流行地区加强媒介控制和监测的迫切需求,以减轻主要对免疫经验不足的人群的登革热负担。

news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织(WHO)于2026年11月4日13:00至14:00(中欧时间)举行网络研讨会,发布了登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒和黄热病的临床管理指南。该活动标题为‘世界卫生组织(WHO)健康紧急事件EPI-WIN网络研讨会:发布登革热、基孔肯雅热、寨卡病毒和黄热病临床管理指南’,于2026年10月27日通过新闻稿公布。这些指南是WHO全球努力应对这些疾病相关健康风险的一部分。网络研讨会由WHO主办,内容为一项确认的举措,未报告具体病例数或暴露人数。该活动是WHO更广泛战略的一部分,旨在改善对登革热等蚊媒病毒疾病的公共卫生应对,强调临床管理和准备的重要性。

Search|t Updates Countries Disasters Organizations Topics Jobs Training Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA World + 15 more Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 27 October 2026 Format Map Source SPC Posted 27 Oct 2026 Originally published 27 Oct 2026 Attachments Download Map (PDF | 512.83 KB) Highlights/updates since the last map was sent on PacNet on 20 October 2026: Dengue • Samoa: Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 78, covering EpiWeek 41 (05 to 11 October 2026), reports 14 new cases, down 78% on the previous week (64 cases), with no laboratory-confirmed case, no new admission and no death. Since 01 January 2025, 20,388 clinically diagnosed cases, 5,547 laboratory-confirmed cases and nine dengue-related deaths have been recorded. DENV-1 accounts for 52% and DENV-2 for 48% of serotyped cases, and children under 15 years for 73% of cases. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: Ministry of Health Samoa, Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 78 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 21 October 2026. Measles • Papua New Guinea: The National Department of Health weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 42 (12 to 18 October 2026) now reports two confirmed measles cases in 2026 (New Ireland 1, Western Highlands 1), against three (East Sepik 2, New Ireland 1) in the EpiWeek 41 bulletin, after the Expert Review Group recategorised cases with recent immunisation or a clinically incompatible presentation. Nineteen IgM-positive measles results have been recorded this year, and the last IgM-positive onset date remains 15 September 2026. Acute fever and rash cases rose from 18 to 33 nationally in EpiWeek 42: National Capital District 16, Eastern Highlands 11, Enga 4, East New Britain and Simbu 1 each (426 cases and 396 samples tested year to date). The measles-rubella vaccination campaign continues to target all children under seven in every district with a detected case, through opportunistic routine immunisation. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Papua New Guinea. – Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health, Public Health Events Weekly Bulletin shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 23 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • New Caledonia: The Department of Health and Social Affairs (DASS) influenza bulletin 2026 #11 of 23 October 2026 reports that the epidemic continues but is now decreasing: 93 laboratory-confirmed cases in EpiWeek 42 (12 to 18 October), against 131 in week 41 and the peak of 151 in week 40. Test positivity remains very high at 57% (55% in week 41), and DASS advises caution as the decrease may partly reflect the school holidays. A(H1N1)pdm09 remains largely predominant (57 of 93 cases), and no new A(H3N2) case had been detected up to 22 October. Emergency department presentations fell from 1,865 in week 41 to 1,505 in week 42 and the share of acute respiratory infections from 13% to 7%, mainly influenza (39%) and pneumonia (26%). Severity remains marked with 33% of patients presenting with influenza-like illness were hospitalised in week 42 (35 patients), against 28% in week 41. Intensive care bed occupancy has been below the 80% vigilance threshold since 20 October and stood at 56% on 22 October. The red alert for influenza A remains in effect for New Caledonia. – Source: New Caledonia Directorate of Health and Social Affairs, Vigilance DASS bulletin 2026-#11 on the influenza epidemic shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 26 October 2026. • New Zealand: For the week ending 18 October 2026, influenza remained the most commonly detected virus among SARI patients in the Auckland region (11 positive samples, followed by rhinovirus with 9). SARI influenza test positivity fell from 25.0 to 20.4%, and positivity among sentinel GP influenza-like illness cases from 18.2 to 6.7%. In 2026, 24.0% of SARI samples (687 of 2,860) and 18.9% of sentinel GP samples (225 of 1,190) have been influenza-positive. Among influenza-positive SARI patients, 39.4% had A(H1) and 32.0% A(H3). The blue alert for influenza A remains in effect for New Zealand. – Source: New Zealand acute respiratory illness dashboard accessed on 27 October 2026. • Vanuatu: The Ministry of Health has declared an influenza A outbreak on Efate Island, Shefa Province, following increased influenza-like illness (ILI) activity and laboratory-confirmed influenza A cases. According to the Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Shefa Province has recorded 1,709 ILI cases against an alert threshold of 223, with weekly cases rising from 360 in EpiWeek 39 to 535 in EpiWeek 42. Children under five account for 57% of ILI cases. Twenty-seven influenza A cases had been confirmed (2 in week 41, 25 in week 42), ten patients had been hospitalised, seven of them discharged, and no death has been reported. Vanuatu National Hospital has activated its emergency operations centre, set up separate triage for flu-like symptoms and restricted visitors. Nationally, the syndromic surveillance bulletin for EpiWeek 42 (12 to 18 October) records 1,185 ILI cases, up from 964 in week 41 and above the alert threshold. Twenty-eight samples were positive for influenza A. A red alert for influenza A is issued for Vanuatu. – Sources: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, via Health Promotions Vanuatu, accessed on 27 October 2026 and Vanuatu Syndromic and Vaccine Preventable Disease Surveillance Bulletin shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 26 October 2026. Rotavirus • Federated States of Micronesia: The Yap weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 42 (12 to 18 October 2026) shows diarrhoea on alert for a ninth consecutive week, with 9 cases, above the alert threshold of 7. Enteric pathogens were identified in four patients: the BioFire gastrointestinal panel found co-infections in three (Salmonella, EAEC, EPEC and ETEC), and one more was positive for adenovirus by rapid test. A public health advisory on diarrhoeal illness remains in place. The blue alert for rotavirus remains in effect for the Federated States of Micronesia (Yap State). – Source: Yap State Department of Health Services, Communicable Disease Weekly Bulletin shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 23 October 2026. Other Information: Dengue • Hawai’i: On 22 October 2026, the Hawaiʻi Department of Health reported a new travel-related dengue case on Maui, with no link to previous cases. It is the tenth dengue case reported in Hawaiʻi in 2026, and the risk of local transmission is considered low. – Source: Hawaiʻi Department of Health, DOH reports 10th travel-related dengue virus case of 2026, accessed on 27 October 2026. One Health - Shamonda virus • France: On 23 October 2026, the French Ministry of Health and Santé publique France reported the first detection of a human infection with Shamonda virus in France. The patient, severely immunocompromised and treated in Lyon for a severe neurological illness, died. Shamonda is an orthobunyavirus transmitted between animals by Culicoides biting midges and mainly affects ruminants. A new lineage has spread in European livestock since summer 2026 and had been detected in cattle in 52 departments as of 20 October. The virus was not previously known to infect humans. The bite of an infected midge is the favoured hypothesis, no human-to-human transmission has been identified and no risk for the general population has been found. A One Health investigation is ongoing. – Sources: Ministère de la Santé, Virus Shamonda : une première détection chez l’être humain and Santé publique France, Virus Shamonda : un premier cas humain détecté en France accessed on 27 October 2026. Latest Updates Panama Panamá: Terremoto en Azuero y Veraguas - Informe de Situación No. 07 (al 28 de octubre 2026, 13:30pm) Vanuatu Vanuatu Anticipatory Action Framework: Tropical Cyclones Ukraine + 1 more Ukraine, Moldova | DG ECHO-funded humanitarian assistance update - DG ECHO Daily Map | 28/10/2026 Colombia + 1 more Colombia: Briefing Departamental, Chocó, enero a diciembre de 2025

A public health advisory on diarrhoeal illness remains in place. The blue alert for rotavirus remains in effect for the Federated States of Micronesia (Yap State). – Source: Yap State Department of Health Services, Communicable Disease Weekly Bulletin shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 23 October 2026. Other Information: Dengue • Hawai’i: On 22 October 2026, the Hawaiʻi Department of Health reported a new travel-related dengue case on Maui, with no link to previous cases. It is the tenth dengue case reported in Hawaiʻi in 2026, and the risk of local transmission is considered low. – Source: Hawaiʻi Department of Health, DOH reports 10th travel-related dengue virus case of 2026, accessed on 27 October 2026. One Health - Shamonda virus • France: On 23 October 2026, the French Ministry of Health and Santé publique France reported the first detection of a human infection with Shamonda virus in France. The patient, severely immunocompromised and treated in Lyon for a severe neurological illness, died. Shamonda is an orthobunyavirus transmitted between animals by Culicoides biting midges and mainly affects ruminants. A new lineage has spread in European livestock since summer 2026 and had been detected in cattle in 52 departments as of 20 October. The virus was not previously known to infect humans. The bite of an infected midge is the favoured hypothesis, no human-to-human transmission has been identified and no risk for the general population has been found. A One Health investigation is ongoing. – Sources: Ministère de la Santé, Virus Shamonda : une première détection chez l’être humain and Santé publique France, Virus Shamonda : un premier cas humain détecté en France accessed on 27 October 2026. supplementary_news.content: Clinical Hub News & Perspective Tools & Reference CME/CE More EN RegisterLog In Ask AI Search AI Mode Medscape Medical NewsFeatures Florida Tallies Highest Locally Acquired Dengue Cases in 100 Years Alicia Ault October 23, 2026 0 1 Add to Email Alerts Jump to Key Points As the number of locally acquired dengue cases in Florida has risen to levels not seen in almost a century, the CDC held a call for clinicians to inform them on how to spot signs of the mosquito-borne illness and how to treat infected individuals. Dengue, known as “breakbone fever” because of the severity of aches and pains associated with infection, is spread through the bite of mosquitoes — primarily the daytime-feeding Aedes aegypti — infected with the virus. The illness is common in tropical and subtropical areas worldwide, and incidence has skyrocketed over the past two decades, fueled in part by climate change, according to the World Health Organization. On the call, CDC officials said that as of October 15, Florida had reported 368 locally acquired cases in eight counties. “This is the largest locally acquired dengue outbreak in Florida since the 1930s,” said Laura Adams, DVM, MPH, epidemiologist with the Dengue Branch at the CDC’s National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases. There are four dengue virus types; most Florida infections have been with dengue virus serotype 2, said Adams. Cases have been reported in all age groups, but most have been in adults aged 30-49 years. Half are in men. SUGGESTED FOR YOU About 47% of those infected required hospitalization, said Adams. The Florida Department of Health is reporting an even greater number of cases. As of October 17, the state had tallied 425 locally acquired dengue cases in 11 counties. The greatest number — 346 — have been in Hillsborough County, which encompasses Tampa. Pinellas County, which includes St. Petersburg, has reported 51 cases. By comparison, Florida had reported 650 locally acquired cases from 2010 to 2025, according to historic CDC data. Hillsborough, Pinellas, and Pasco counties have repeatedly extended dengue-related states of emergency to shift funds into aerial spraying to kill mosquito larvae. Until this year, cases had also been rising in Texas, California, Arizona, and Hawaii, but none of those states have reported any locally acquired illness in 2026. Virginia, however, reported its first locally acquired case earlier in the year, said Adams. Six US territories and freely associated states also have frequent or continuous dengue transmission: Puerto Rico, American Samoa, the US Virgin Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau. Older adults and those with comorbidities such as asthma, diabetes, obesity, and hypertension are at higher risk for dengue. Pregnancy has been associated with a higher risk for progression to severe disease, Adams said, adding that a second dengue infection also increases severity risk, but not a third or fourth infection. Abrupt-Onset Fever and Rash About 3-14 days after being bitten by an infected mosquito, the 20%-40% of people who become symptomatic will have an abrupt fever, nausea and vomiting, mucosal bleeding, cough and sore throat, rash, and marked flushing of the face, neck, and chest. Patients might also develop a macular or maculopapular rash that starts on the trunk and spreads across the face and limbs, said Liliana Sánchez-González, MD, MPH, CTropMed, of the CDC’s National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases, on the call. Most patients seek care during this febrile phase, which can last 2-7 days, she said. They are also viremic during this phase. If the fever abates, most patients improve. Some might present with or develop more severe symptoms, which constitute warning signs that the patient might slip into a more critical phase. Those patients may have abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, ascites, altered mental status, and a progressive increase in hematocrit. “Any mucosal bleeding is a warning sign in dengue, and it is important to ask about bleeding that might not be obvious during the physical examination, including changes in the color of the urine or stools and changes in menstrual flow,” said Sánchez-González. About 5% of those who are infected and symptomatic develop severe dengue, which is marked by plasma leakage and can lead to shock, respiratory distress, severe bleeding, and damage to the heart, brain, and liver. Supportive Care Is the Main Treatment There is currently no approved dengue vaccine that’s available in the US, so prevention is primarily achieved through eliminating mosquito breeding areas and telling people to use insecticides and clothing to ward off bites. There are diagnostics available through state and local health departments and some private labs, said Sánchez-González. A reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction test combined with an immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody test, or a dengue nonstructural protein 1 antigen test plus IgM, can detect dengue within 7 days of symptom onset. A negative result does not rule out infection. IgM antibodies are detectable for up to 90 days, so it is the recommended diagnostic test after a week. But, said Sánchez-González, “clinical management should not be delayed while waiting for laboratory confirmation.” The standard of care for dengue is supportive management — primarily administering intravenous fluids and strictly monitoring intake and outflow — as there is no curative. Patients with severe dengue may require emergency treatment that includes oxygen and close monitoring of hematocrit. Dengue patients should never be given corticosteroids, as there is no evidence of utility, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, as they could increase bleeding risk, said Sánchez-González. The agency also recommends against intramuscular injections or prophylactic platelet transfusions. CDC has created a dengue clinical management pocket guide that provides algorithms for outpatient and inpatient management. Alicia Ault is a Saint Petersburg, Florida-based freelance journalist whose work has appeared in many health and science publications, including Smithsonian.com. You can find her on X @aliciaault and on Bluesky @aliciaault.bsky.social. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, October 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Mosquito Saliva Protein Fragment Boosts Dengue Virus Replication in Immune Cells by October 28, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Mosquito Saliva Protein Fragment Boosts Dengue Virus Replication in Immune Cells Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A laboratory study has pinpointed the precise region of an Aedes albopictus salivary protein that binds dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) and enhances its replication in immune cells. The protein, known as 34k2, was already known to promote DENV-2 infection, but the functional domain responsible had remained undefined. The new work, published in Parasites & Vectors, identifies the C-terminal portion of the protein as the viral-binding site and shows that this fragment alone is sufficient to potentiate viral replication and alter inflammatory signaling. The researchers used AlphaFold3 structural prediction and ZDOCK molecular docking to localize the interaction interfaces between 34k2 and DENV-2 virions. From these predictions they constructed two truncated variants: an N-terminal fragment designated rAlb-34k2-I and a C-terminal fragment designated rAlb-34k2-II, corresponding to residues 148 to 322 of the full protein. Surface plasmon resonance measured how tightly each fragment bound to DENV-2 particles. The binding results were decisive. The C-terminal fragment rAlb-34k2-II bound DENV-2 virions with high affinity, with a reported dissociation constant of 2.88 nanomolar, while the N-terminal fragment rAlb-34k2-I showed no measurable binding. This asymmetry indicates that the viral-binding capability of 34k2 resides specifically within its C-terminal region rather than being distributed across the protein. Functional assays followed in two human and mouse immune cell lines: RAW264.7 macrophages and THP-1 monocytes. When cells were pre-incubated with rAlb-34k2-II before viral exposure, the fragment significantly enhanced DENV-2 replication and the production of infectious plaque-forming virus, as assessed by immunofluorescence, plaque assays and quantitative RT-PCR. These are in vitro cell culture findings, so they demonstrate a mechanism in isolated cells rather than an effect measured directly in human infection. Beyond facilitating replication, the salivary fragment reshaped the inflammatory response of the immune cells. Both rAlb-34k2-II and the full-length rAlb-34k2 protein significantly upregulated the transcription of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-1β and the chemokines CCL2 and CXCL2 in vitro, measured by qPCR and ELISA. The response followed a distinctive kinetic pattern: a transient early spike in inflammatory cytokines was followed by sustained expression of chemokines. To extend the findings beyond cell culture, the team used a murine footpad injection model. Injection of the full-length 34k2 protein into the footpad induced a pro-inflammatory profile in the local tissue that was consistent with the in vitro results, supporting the idea that the protein’s immunomodulatory activity operates in living tissue and not only in cultured cells. The authors conclude that the C-terminal fragment of Ae. albopictus 34k2 constitutes a high-affinity viral-binding domain that potentiates DENV-2 replication and modulates host inflammation. They propose that targeting this specific salivary–viral interface could support the development of competitive decoy peptides or next-generation salivary-based vaccines aimed at interrupting arboviral transmission. Such applications remain proposals at this stage; the study did not test decoy peptides or vaccines, and the reported effects come from structural predictions, cell culture experiments and a local murine injection model rather than from efficacy trials. The work is presented as an early-access, peer-reviewed accepted article, citable with a permanent DOI and subject to further edits before the final version of record. Its mechanistic contribution is to narrow a broad observation—that mosquito saliva can facilitate arboviral infection—down to a defined 175-residue domain, and to link that binding activity to a measurable shift in cytokine and chemokine expression. If subsequent research confirms the interface in vivo and develops inhibitors against it, the finding could inform strategies against dengue, a disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes whose saliva proteins are increasingly studied as modulators of viral infection and host immunity. Subject of Research: Identification of the C-terminal viral-binding domain of the Aedes albopictus salivary protein 34k2 and its effects on DENV-2 replication and host inflammation. 病毒性传染病患病率不断上升,对全球公共卫生构成重大威胁。其中,登革病毒(dengue virus, DENV)是最广泛传播的虫媒病毒感染之一,每年影响近4亿人;据世界卫生组织(World Health Organization, WHO)报告,约1%病例出现严重临床表现。学术和产业界围绕DENV的分子病毒学、流行病学模式、传播途径和治疗靶点开展了广泛研究。四价CYD-TDV(Dengvaxia)疫苗的开发标志着登革热预防的重要进展。然而,新出现的证据显示当前疫苗接种策略存在若干局限性,促使研究人员日益重视抗病毒药物的发现和开发,作为有效登革热管理的替代或补充治疗选择。共发现14种主要生物活性化合物与登革热高度相关,在登革热与生物活性化合物之间获得70个共同靶点。通过KEGG(Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes)和Metascape分析进行的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用(protein–protein interaction, PPI)和网络通路分析显示,DENV-2靶点具有较高相关性。分子对接(molecular docking)分析显示,Globulol和Ecalyptol与两个受体1oke和1tg8 f DENV-2具有较高结合亲和力,结合能分别为?8.3和?7.6。毒性和成药性(drug-likeness)分析证实这些代谢物用于药物开发的安全性。这些发现提示蓝桉(Eucalyptus globulus)精油可能具有治疗登革热的潜力。然而,仍需使用动物模型开展进一步体内(in vivo)研究以验证其治疗效力。 研究背景与意义:登革病毒(dengue virus, DENV)属黄病毒科,含DENV-1至DENV-4四个血清型,主要由埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)传播。全球近五分之二人口受威胁,每年约3.9亿感染,约50万需住院、约2万死亡;自2000年登革热(dengue fever, DF)发病率显著上升并扩展至129个国家。当前尚无获批治疗药物或有效疫苗;四价CYD-TDV(Dengvaxia)疫苗虽为关键进展,但有效性有限且不良反应限制使用,因此抗病毒药物发现成为替代或补充策略。蓝桉(Eucalyptus globulus)精油含Eucalyptol等成分,已有抗病毒、抗菌、抗炎和抗氧化报道;为明确其抗登革热潜力,研究人员开展GC-MS成分表征、杀幼虫活性评价及网络药理学和分子对接分析,以筛选其生物活性成分对DENV-2受体的作用。研究结论提示Globulol和Eucalyptol等具较高结合亲和力,毒性/成药性较好,蓝桉精油可能作为抗登革热天然候选来源,但需体内动物模型验证。 欢迎下载《揭秘单细胞测序》深入了解这一改变科研方法的新技术领 取 关键技术方法(≤250字):样本来源:蓝桉叶采自巴基斯坦Rawalpindi地区,由Arid Agriculture University, Rawalpindi, Pakistan植物学系专家鉴定。研究人员采用光伏(PV)驱动水蒸气蒸馏提取精油,GC-MS(gas chromatography–mass spectrometry,气相色谱-质谱联用;PerkinElmer Clarus 500,NIST11.L库)分析成分;以埃及伊蚊IV龄幼虫进行杀幼虫生物测定(62.5–1000 ppm,Temephos阳性对照,probit分析LC50与LC90);用SwissTargetPrediction、DisGeNET、GeneCards、DAVID、STRING、KEGG和Metascape开展网络药理学与富集分析;用AutoDock Vina对DENV-2受体1TG8和1OKE进行分子对接,并以ProSA、Ramachandran和MolProbity评估模型;用Protox-III、Lipinski五规则和SwissADME评估毒性与成药性。 3.1 Larvicidal Activity of E. globulus Essential Oil Against Ades Aegypti:通过24、48、72、96和120 h暴露及62.5–1000 ppm浓度梯度,死亡率呈时间与剂量依赖:24 h为33%–73%,48 h为46%–80%,72 h为60%–80%,96 h为66.6%–86.6%,120 h为70%–90%;结论为精油对埃及伊蚊幼虫具杀灭活性。 3.2 Phytochemical Profiling of E. globulus Essential Oil:通过PV蒸汽蒸馏和GC-MS,10 kg叶得约45 mL精油,鉴定25种化合物;D-Limonene与Eucalyptol合计>80%,均属terpenoid(monoterpenoids和sesquiterpenoids),并含(?)-Globulol、Longifolene等,为后续分析提供成分基础。 3.3 Metabolite and Disease Targets:通过SwissTargetPrediction预测,代谢物靶点多与信号、免疫、炎症和外源刺激相关;D-Limonene关联核受体、Family A GPCR(G蛋白偶联受体)、CYP450(细胞色素P450)和代谢酶,Eucalyptol关联CYP450、转移酶、氧化还原酶、水解酶和裂解酶,Thymol关联电压门控离子通道、氧化还原酶和GPCR;提示多靶点潜力。 3.4 Metabolite-Disease Common Targets:通过DisGeNET和GeneCards疾病靶点与代谢物靶点交叉,获得70个共同靶点;CD38和MAPK14为关键重叠基因,涉及免疫细胞信号、细胞因子产生、钙动员、p38 MAPK应激/炎症/免疫调节及病毒复制相关过程。 3.5 Gene Ontology (GO) Analysis:通过DAVID GO(Gene Ontology,基因本体)富集,分子功能(MF)中heterocyclic compound binding的p值为9.818×10?13、chemokine ligand binding为6.436×10?3;生物学过程(BP)富集于viral processes(p=2.486×10?3)及T细胞谱系定向、T细胞稳态和白细胞介导免疫;细胞组分(CC)富集于线粒体膜和细胞器外膜,提示靶点集中于病毒过程与免疫应答。 3.6 Pathway Enrichment Analysis:通过KEGG(Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes)和Metascape通路富集,共同靶点富集于VEGF(血管内皮生长因子)信号、sphingolipid信号、IL-17(白细胞介素-17)信号、T细胞信号和platelet activation;37%靶点与登革热高度相关,提示应激信号与免疫激活相关。 3.7 Molecular Docking Analysis:通过AutoDock Vina对接1OKE(DENV-2包膜蛋白结构域III)和1TG8(NS3(非结构蛋白3)丝氨酸蛋白酶),正文称Globulol和Eucalyptol对1OKE具较高结合亲和力(Globulol ?8.3 kcal/mol、Eucalyptol ?7.6 kcal/mol),Eucalyptol对1TG8为?7.6 kcal/mol、Limonene为?6.8 kcal/mol;原文正文与表格对个别配体—受体对应数值存在差异,解读时保留原文数值;结论提示这些成分可能干扰病毒附着/融合或NS3蛋白酶活性。 3.8 Toxicity Prediction and Lipinski Rule of Five:通过Protox-III和Lipinski五规则,Eucalyptol与Globulol对肝毒性、神经毒性、心脏毒性和致癌性均预测为inactive;Thymol和Longifolene对神经毒性部分active,Limonene对心脏毒性轻度active;LD50最高为Longifolene 5000 mg/kg,其次Limonene 4400 mg/kg、Eucalyptol 2480 mg/kg;所选代谢物均无Lipinski规则violation,提示安全性和成药性。 3.9 Swiss ADME Analysis:通过SwissADME(absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion,吸收、分布、代谢、排泄)分析,所有代谢物位于colored zone,提示口服生物利用度适宜。 讨论部分总结:原文指出药用植物是药物发现的重要来源,网络药理学整合系统生物学、生物信息学和药理学,可从“一药一靶”转向“多成分—多靶点—多通路”。登革热尚无特异抗病毒治疗,Dengvaxia有效性和不良反应受限;蓝桉长期用作驱蚊,Eucalyptol等为重要成分。原文认为杀幼虫的时间/剂量依赖毒性与Eucalyptol、Limonene、Globulol等可能靶向GABA(γ-氨基丁酸)受体或章鱼胺能受体有关;70个共同靶点、GO中response to chemical和heterocyclic compound binding富集、Metascape登革热相关富集及分子对接结果共同支持其抗DENV-2潜力。 研究结论翻译:登革病毒感染全球负担日益加重,凸显对有效抗病毒药物的迫切需求。本研究通过综合的计算机模拟(in silico)分析,从蓝桉精油中鉴定出14种与登革热具有潜在治疗相关性的主要生物活性化合物。网络药理学和通路富集分析显示其与DENV-2靶点显著相关。分子对接表明Globulol和Eucalyptol对关键病毒蛋白(1OKE和1TG8)具有较强结合亲和力,提示潜在抑制活性。毒性和成药性评估证实这些代谢物的安全性,支持其进一步药物开发候选资格。总体而言,这些发现突出蓝桉精油作为抗登革热天然来源的潜力,值得通过适当动物模型进一步体内验证。 India Advertisement Why Kadayanallur pilot is crucial for India’s dengue vaccine rollout Public health expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya explains Qdenga’s efficacy, safety concerns, India’s indigenous dengue vaccine candidate and why surveillance and mosquito control remain essential Lavanya Prabhakaran 23 Oct 2026 12:32 PM Click the Play button to hear this message in audio format Dengue remains a major public health challenge in India, with gaps in diagnosis and reporting making the actual disease burden difficult to estimate. With Takeda’s Qdenga vaccine receiving regulatory approval in India and an implementation pilot planned in Tamil Nadu’s Kadayanallur, in Tenkasi district, questions remain about its safety, effectiveness and suitability for wider public vaccination. Advertisement × PLAYSTREAM 00:00 StayNext 00:00 Ad will close in:click to close Speaking to The Federal, public health specialist and vaccines expert Dr Chandrakant Lahariya discusses the evidence behind Qdenga, the lessons from earlier dengue vaccines, the progress of India’s indigenous vaccine candidate Dengyol, and how the Kadayanallur initiative could help prepare the country for a broader rollout. Edited excerpts: Where does dengue stand in India today in terms of cases, deaths and geographical spread? Is India's current dengue surveillance strong enough to measure the impact of a vaccine? Nearly two decades ago, it was largely associated with major cities and metropolitan areas, but today dengue is spreading into rural areas. The disease surveillance, including dengue surveillance, remains suboptimal in the country despite National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control (NCVBDC)’s official figures. Also read: Dengue: TN records 15,796 cases this year, highest in India Official figures recorded around three lakh dengue cases and 500 deaths in 2023. In 2024, the reported numbers were approximately 2.5 lakh to 3 lakh cases and around 300 deaths. By September this year, approximately 1.2 lakh cases and 130 deaths had been reported. These figures do not reflect the actual disease burden, but they provide an indication of its scale, as underdiagnosis and underreporting remain significant challenges. India has been working to improve disease surveillance through initiatives such as the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme and laboratory networks. However, many people seek treatment in the private sector, where reporting remains relatively poor. Surveillance in rural areas is also inadequate. The introduction of a dengue vaccine presents a valuable opportunity for India to strengthen its dengue surveillance system. How important is the Kadayanallur pilot programme and what results is it expected to generate? India's drug regulator, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), has granted marketing authorisation for Qdenga, the dengue vaccine developed by Takeda. The vaccine can now be considered for introduction in the country, subject to the relevant implementation decisions. However, before a vaccine is introduced more widely, it is important to understand the practical challenges involved in delivering it on the ground. Such initiatives help assess operational feasibility, identify challenges and understand public responses to vaccination. They also provide an opportunity to identify communication gaps and determine the training requirements of healthcare workers. The clinical trials required before regulatory approval would already have been conducted globally. Qdenga has received regulatory approval in more than 35 countries, and India's regulator has also approved it. The immediate requirement is to understand how the vaccine can be delivered effectively through the public health system. Advertisement The initiative should also provide early indications of adverse events and how effectively they are managed. Also read: Kerala reports 3 more communicable disease deaths; Shigella cases at 59 The findings from Kadayanallur could offer useful guidance when Tamil Nadu and other Indian states consider introducing the dengue vaccine. What does the available evidence say about Qdenga's safety and effectiveness? Which concerns are legitimate, and how does the vaccine work against the different dengue serotypes? Qdenga, also known as TAK-003, is a live-attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine. This means it contains weakened dengue viruses designed to stimulate an immune response without causing the disease in the way a natural infection would. The vaccine targets all four dengue virus serotypes: DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4. Following clinical trials, the recommended schedule consists of two subcutaneous injections administered three months apart. In July, India's CDSCO approved Qdenga for individuals aged four to 60 years. However, regulatory approval does not automatically mean that a vaccine should be included in the national immunisation programme. The decision to introduce it into a public health programme requires a separate assessment of operational feasibility and public health priorities. The Phase III clinical trials of Qdenga were conducted across countries in Asia and Latin America, enrolling approximately 20,000 children and adolescents. The vaccine demonstrated an efficacy of 80.2 per cent against laboratory-confirmed symptomatic dengue. It also reduced hospitalisation by approximately 90 per cent among vaccinated participants compared with those who were not vaccinated. Follow-up data extending to four and a half years after the second dose showed that the vaccine retained an efficacy of 61.2 per cent against symptomatic dengue and 84 per cent against dengue-related hospitalisation. These results indicate that Qdenga can provide meaningful protection against dengue. However, its safety profile must continue to be monitored, particularly as vaccination expands to larger populations. What are the possible side effects of Qdenga? So far, Qdenga has shown a favourable safety profile. However, some minor adverse events can occur, including pain at the injection site, headaches, muscle aches, fatigue and temporary fever. One rare but serious adverse event is anaphylaxis, a potentially life-threatening allergic reaction that requires immediate medical attention. Also read: Bharat Biotech, Gavi-UNICEF deal to cut malaria vaccine price by 40 pc Brazil's post-marketing surveillance found that approximately 1.4 million doses of Qdenga had been administered, with 43 reported cases of anaphylaxis. This translates to around 3.3 cases per 100,000 doses. None of those reported cases was fatal. This experience indicates that, with effective emergency response systems and adequate preparedness, such reactions can be managed. Although anaphylaxis is potentially life-threatening, timely recognition and appropriate treatment are essential. Another concern with dengue vaccines is the possibility of vaccine-associated enhanced dengue. This refers to the potential for a subsequent natural dengue infection to become more severe in some vaccinated individuals. This concern emerged with earlier dengue vaccines, and it remains important to monitor for such outcomes with Qdenga. What lessons should India draw from countries such as Brazil, where Qdenga has already been introduced? When India plans a dengue vaccination programme, it can draw on lessons from previous immunisation initiatives, while also learning from the experiences of Brazil and other countries where Qdenga is being used. The process should be guided by experts and public health specialists to ensure that implementation decisions are based on evidence. It is important to consider not only the vaccine's clinical efficacy but also the practical requirements of delivering it to eligible populations, maintaining the cold chain, training healthcare workers and communicating effectively with the public. These considerations will determine how successfully the vaccine can be integrated into India's existing public health infrastructure. How is Qdenga different from Dengvaxia and what should India watch for? Dengvaxia was not licensed in India, although it was approved in other countries. It demonstrated efficacy against all four dengue serotypes, but a major safety concern emerged involving what is known as antibody-dependent enhancement. One key difference between the two vaccines is their underlying viral backbone. Dengvaxia was developed using a yellow fever virus backbone, whereas Qdenga uses a dengue virus serotype 2 backbone. Also read: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda, patient dies Qdenga has demonstrated protection against symptomatic dengue in clinical trial populations that included both people who had previously been infected with dengue and those who had not. So far, the antibody-dependent enhancement concern associated with Dengvaxia has not been established with Qdenga. As Qdenga is introduced into new populations, Indian health authorities must maintain strong surveillance to identify any unexpected safety signals, including severe dengue following vaccination and subsequent natural infection. How close is India’s indigenous vaccine DengiAll to roll out? India is making encouraging progress with its indigenous dengue vaccine candidate, DengiAll, being developed by Panacea Biotec in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). The vaccine is undergoing Phase III clinical trials. Like Qdenga, DengiAll is a live-attenuated, tetravalent dengue vaccine. It uses dengue virus strains originally licensed from the US National Institutes of Health. One potentially important difference is the dosing schedule. Qdenga requires two doses administered three months apart, whereas DengiAll is being developed as a single-dose vaccine. If the single-dose vaccine proves safe and effective, it could offer considerable logistical advantages. Panacea Biotec announced in January 2026 that enrolment had been completed. Participants are to be followed for two years after receiving the vaccine or placebo to evaluate efficacy, safety and immunogenicity. An indigenous vaccine could potentially improve the availability of doses and offer advantages in affordability. denguedengue vaccinedengue symptomspublic health expert About the AuthorLavanya Prabhakaran Lavanya Prabhakaran is Assistant Editor with The Federal. supplementary_news.content_title: Human Dengue Study Reveals How Preexisting Immunity Shapes Secondary Infections
supplementary_news.content: Dengue [BlackJack3D / iStock / Getty Images Plus] Roughly half of the world’s population is now at risk of dengue, with an estimated 100–400 million infections occurring each year. The viral infection (also known as break-bone fever) is more common in tropical and subtropical areas of the world. Currently, prevention relies on control of the mosquito vector that transmits the virus. Dengue virus has a particularly unique challenges, and is especially pernicious compared with many other viruses, as secondary infections can be worse than the first. Now, a new Phase I trial involving controlled infections in human volunteers provides new details about how preexisting immunity and anti-dengue antibodies affect the nature of secondary infections with dengue. The work is published in Science Translational Medicine in the paper, “Dengue virus controlled human challenge reveals that preexisting immunity shapes viral replication and broadly protective responses.” The findings are among the first to glean insights using a large controlled human challenge, and could inform future therapeutics and the design of more broadly protective vaccines. Secondary infections with dengue are often the most severe ones because preexisting antibodies can boost viral counts and raise the risk of severe symptoms. This has frustrated the development of badly needed vaccines for dengue. Furthermore, it’s been challenging to understand how pre-infection affects dengue outcomes, as animal models have many limitations and patients usually don’t present until after viral counts have peaked. In this study, researchers recruited 45 healthy adults who had either zero, one, or more than one prior infection with any of the four strains of dengue virus (DENV1-DENV4). The volunteers received injections of a live, weakened strain of DENV3 in a challenge study, allowing the researchers to fully interrogate dengue immunity dynamics in humans in a safe and controlled setting. The findings led to various conclusions: for example, people whose antibodies boosted the replication of the virus had the highest viral counts and waning of CD8-bearing T cells and antibodies. Additionally, people who had higher amounts of antibodies against the viral nonstructural protein 1 displayed more balanced immune responses and lower viral counts. More specifically, the authors write, “Viremia was associated with more, but still mild, clinical signs and symptoms, and secondary infection resulted in greater viremia, neutralizing antibodies, and protective T cell responses. However, those whose baseline antibodies most efficiently increased dengue virus replication in an in vitro assay experienced delayed inflammatory and adaptive immune activation, the highest viremia, strong acute immune responses, and waning of potent CD8+ T cells and antibodies. In contrast, higher baseline antibodies against the nonstructural protein 1 of multiple serotypes predicted early interferon and balanced immune activation, viremia control, and development of enduring, potent B and T cells, revealing how vaccines can induce broad, long-­lasting protection.” “Collectively, this work confirms multiple hypotheses generated by natural history studies and reveals the optimal conditions for inducing potent and persistent immunity against DENV1 to DENV4,” they note. Luis Robayo/AFP/Getty Images Zachary Stieber Senior Reporter 10/28/2026|Updated: 10/28/2026 0:00 X 1 The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has launched an emergency response to the surge in Florida of cases of dengue, a disease caused by a mosquito-borne virus, the agency confirmed on Oct. 28. “CDC is working with public health leadership to support the dengue outbreak response,” Laura Adams, commander in the U.S. Public Health Service and an epidemiologist with the CDC’s Dengue Branch, told The Epoch Times via email. The activation of the level 3 emergency response was done to provide additional support to Florida and the Republic of the Marshall Islands, which are dealing with dengue outbreaks, “as well as to prepare for possible increased transmission in other areas of the United States,” Adams said. The activation means the CDC is deploying its own staff, including personnel from the CDC’s Emergency Operations Center, to affected areas, and enables the coordination of activities such as epidemiologic investigations and laboratory testing. The CDC is deploying entomologists, epidemiologists, and laboratory experts to Florida to help with trapping mosquitoes, investigating cases, and optimizing lab equipment, Adams said. The CDC has sent personnel to the Marshall Islands to help with the outbreak response, including training local workers and providing rapid tests. Dengue is a disease caused by dengue viruses, which are spread to people through mosquito bites. Symptoms can include aches and pains, nausea, and rash. The disease is fatal in a small percentage of cases. Related Stories Florida Reports Dozens More Cases of Mosquito-Borne Dengue Virus CDC Deputy Director Departing Just Months After Appointment There is one vaccine for the disease available in the United States, and it is only recommended for children aged 9 to 16 who have previously had dengue and are living in areas where dengue is common. The best method of prevention is avoiding mosquito bites, according to the CDC, and treatment involves resting, staying hydrated, and taking acetaminophen to control fever and reduce pain. Florida has recorded a surge in dengue cases this year. In its last update, the Florida Department of Health said 425 cases have been locally acquired, primarily in Tampa and the remainder of Hillsborough County. One person, an 80-year-old woman, has died of the disease, officials told local outlets. Another 320 cases associated with travel have been recorded in 2026 in the state. Hillsborough County, Pinellas County, and Pasco County have declared emergencies over the outbreak. They have directed residents to cut down on places mosquitoes congregate, including standing water in tarps and birdbaths; to wear long clothing outside; and to apply insect repellent when leaving the home. The number of cases in Florida is much higher than has been logged in recent years, Adams told clinicians during a recent call. She said that most cases have been caused by dengue virus type 2, and that about half have required hospitalization. Overall, four U.S. jurisdictions, including Puerto Rico, have reported 1,819 locally acquired cases in 2026, according to a CDC database. The Republic of the Marshall Islands, a sovereign nation that the United States assists with defense and other support, has reported hundreds of cases in recent weeks. The president of the nation, comprising islands in the Pacific Ocean southwest of Hawaii, recently declared a state of disaster over the dengue outbreak and the impacts of El Nino conditions. The declaration said that the outbreak “is placing additional demands on government health services, personnel, supplies, and other resources.” We had a problem loading this article. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, October 28, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Mosquito Saliva Protein Fragment Boosts Dengue Virus Replication in Immune Cells by October 28, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Mosquito Saliva Protein Fragment Boosts Dengue Virus Replication in Immune Cells Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A laboratory study has pinpointed the precise region of an Aedes albopictus salivary protein that binds dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) and enhances its replication in immune cells. The protein, known as 34k2, was already known to promote DENV-2 infection, but the functional domain responsible had remained undefined. The new work, published in Parasites & Vectors, identifies the C-terminal portion of the protein as the viral-binding site and shows that this fragment alone is sufficient to potentiate viral replication and alter inflammatory signaling. The researchers used AlphaFold3 structural prediction and ZDOCK molecular docking to localize the interaction interfaces between 34k2 and DENV-2 virions. From these predictions they constructed two truncated variants: an N-terminal fragment designated rAlb-34k2-I and a C-terminal fragment designated rAlb-34k2-II, corresponding to residues 148 to 322 of the full protein. Surface plasmon resonance measured how tightly each fragment bound to DENV-2 particles. The binding results were decisive. The C-terminal fragment rAlb-34k2-II bound DENV-2 virions with high affinity, with a reported dissociation constant of 2.88 nanomolar, while the N-terminal fragment rAlb-34k2-I showed no measurable binding. This asymmetry indicates that the viral-binding capability of 34k2 resides specifically within its C-terminal region rather than being distributed across the protein. Discover more Biology textbook sales Study Biology Learn Engineering Track Biotech Tour Colleges Functional assays followed in two human and mouse immune cell lines: RAW264.7 macrophages and THP-1 monocytes. When cells were pre-incubated with rAlb-34k2-II before viral exposure, the fragment significantly enhanced DENV-2 replication and the production of infectious plaque-forming virus, as assessed by immunofluorescence, plaque assays and quantitative RT-PCR. These are in vitro cell culture findings, so they demonstrate a mechanism in isolated cells rather than an effect measured directly in human infection. Beyond facilitating replication, the salivary fragment reshaped the inflammatory response of the immune cells. Both rAlb-34k2-II and the full-length rAlb-34k2 protein significantly upregulated the transcription of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-1β and the chemokines CCL2 and CXCL2 in vitro, measured by qPCR and ELISA. The response followed a distinctive kinetic pattern: a transient early spike in inflammatory cytokines was followed by sustained expression of chemokines. To extend the findings beyond cell culture, the team used a murine footpad injection model. Injection of the full-length 34k2 protein into the footpad induced a pro-inflammatory profile in the local tissue that was consistent with the in vitro results, supporting the idea that the protein’s immunomodulatory activity operates in living tissue and not only in cultured cells. The authors conclude that the C-terminal fragment of Ae. albopictus 34k2 constitutes a high-affinity viral-binding domain that potentiates DENV-2 replication and modulates host inflammation. They propose that targeting this specific salivary–viral interface could support the development of competitive decoy peptides or next-generation salivary-based vaccines aimed at interrupting arboviral transmission. Such applications remain proposals at this stage; the study did not test decoy peptides or vaccines, and the reported effects come from structural predictions, cell culture experiments and a local murine injection model rather than from efficacy trials. Discover more Genetic testing kits Get Health Tips Health health chemical The work is presented as an early-access, peer-reviewed accepted article, citable with a permanent DOI and subject to further edits before the final version of record. Its mechanistic contribution is to narrow a broad observation—that mosquito saliva can facilitate arboviral infection—down to a defined 175-residue domain, and to link that binding activity to a measurable shift in cytokine and chemokine expression. If subsequent research confirms the interface in vivo and develops inhibitors against it, the finding could inform strategies against dengue, a disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes whose saliva proteins are increasingly studied as modulators of viral infection and host immunity. Request Free Sample Speak to Analyst Dengue outbreaks are accelerating investment in vaccine research, Wolbachia-based mosquito control, advanced diagnostics and surveillance technologies as governments strengthen disease prevention and healthcare preparedness worldwide. Rising dengue infections are accelerating global investment in vaccine research, innovative mosquito-control technologies and integrated disease-prevention strategies. Bangladesh is considering dengue vaccine clinical trials amid a severe 2026 outbreak, while India approved its first dengu vaccine in July 2026. Advances in Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes, biological control and disease surveillance are creating opportunities for pharmaceutical companies, biotechnology researchers and public-health organisations. Dengue is an increasingly significant global healthcare challenge, driven by climate change, urbanisation, population movement and inadequate mosquito-control infrastructure. The World Health Organization (WHO) reported approximately 14.6 million dengue cases and more than 12,000 related deaths in 2024, marking the largest recorded annual outbreak at that time. Recent developments highlight a shift beyond conventional fogging and insecticide spraying towards vaccination, clinical research, improved diagnostics and sustainable vector control. Bangladesh’s consideration of vaccine trials and India’s regulatory approval of Qdenga underscore the growing importance of preventive healthcare investment. However, prevention remains challenging because of four dengue virus serotypes, variations in vaccine performance, affordability constraints and the need for sustained community participation. Consequently, emerging opportunities extend beyond vaccine manufacturers to biotechnology firms, diagnostic developers, mosquito-control technology providers, research institutions and healthcare infrastructure operators, supporting a broader, integrated approach to dengue prevention and control. Why Is Dengue Increasing Global Demand for Preventive Healthcare? Dengue transmission is increasing pressure on healthcare systems, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. Spread primarily by infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the disease thrives in areas with stagnant water and inadequate sanitation. The World Health Organization reported approximately 14.4 million dengue cases and 11,201 deaths globally in 2024, with Brazil and India among the affected countries. Rising infections are encouraging governments to strengthen early diagnosis, disease surveillance and preventive healthcare investments. In Bangladesh, increasing hospitalisations and deaths in 2026 have intensified consideration of dengue vaccine clinical trials. Severe dengue requires hospitalisation and supportive care, increasing healthcare expenditure and demand for medical infrastructure. Opportunities are emerging in vaccine research, diagnostic testing, mosquito-control technologies and digital surveillance. However, commercial growth depends on regulatory approval, affordability, clinical evidence and effectiveness in high-transmission settings. Unlock exclusive market insights. Dengue vaccine research is transforming prevention strategies by combining immunisation, clinical evaluation and public-health surveillance. A laboratory study published in Virology Journal compared how immune cells from older and middle-aged donors respond when exposed to dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2) in culture. The researchers found that cells from older donors released higher amounts of two soluble proteins, galectin-3 and galectin-9, at later time points, while concentrations of most other measured mediators were generally lower. The study used peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) drawn from volunteer donors: ten older donors aged 65 years or above, with a median age of 74.9 years and an observed range of 65.8 to 92.0 years, and ten middle-aged donors, with a median age of 39.4 years and an observed range of 34.8 to 49.1 years. In the laboratory, the PBMCs were exposed to the DENV-2 strain TH-36 at a multiplicity of infection of 5. To track the immune response over time, the team collected culture supernatants before exposure and at 24, 48, and 72 hours after DENV-2 exposure. They then measured nine soluble mediators: GM-CSF, IFN-γ, IL-6, IL-10, MCP-1, TNF-α, and VEGF-A, along with galectin-3 and galectin-9. Discover more Check Symptoms Study Biology Order DNA Kits Donate to Research Study Chemistry The most pronounced differences emerged late in the culture period. Compared with cultures from middle-aged donors, cultures from older donors had higher galectin-3 concentrations at both 48 and 72 hours. At 48 hours, the median galectin-3 concentration was 363.6 pg/mL in older donor cultures versus 197.8 pg/mL in middle-aged donor cultures, with an exploratory p value of 0.0412. By 72 hours, the gap widened: 810.1 pg/mL versus 218.5 pg/mL, with a p value of 0.0011. Galectin-9 followed a similar late pattern. At 72 hours, older donor cultures showed a median concentration of 219.6 pg/mL compared with 92.23 pg/mL in middle-aged donor cultures, a difference that reached a nominal p value of 0.0355. The reported differences in galectin-9 were concentrated at this late time point. In contrast to the galectins, the seven other measured mediators were generally lower in older donor cultures across the 24 to 72 hour window. The authors also noted that IFN-γ, IL-10, and TNF-α differed between the groups even at baseline, before any virus was introduced, indicating that some differences in circulating immune mediator levels were already present in the donors’ blood. The authors frame these findings as exploratory. The between-group p values at each time point were unadjusted comparisons, and interpretation of the nominal significance levels is limited by the small sample size of ten donors per group and by the multiple comparisons performed across nine mediators and four time points. The study also did not test statistical associations between cytokine and galectin concentrations, so the relationship between the two patterns remains an open question. Discover more Get Health Tips Read Med Journals Study Anatomy Compare Lab Gear Biology textbook sales There are further limits on what the results can tell us. The experiments used an ex vivo culture model, in which isolated PBMCs are exposed to virus in a dish rather than within the full complexity of a living immune system. This design cannot establish causal mechanisms or clinical outcomes, and the findings may not translate directly to how older patients respond to dengue infection in the body. Despite these caveats, the study makes a methodological point: the authors conclude that the contrasting pattern highlights the value of examining galectins alongside other soluble mediators when investigating variation in responses to DENV-2. A measurement strategy limited to the standard cytokine panel would not have captured the elevated galectin concentrations observed in the older donor cultures. According to the authors, the small sample and the culture model limit causal and clinical inference, and larger donor-linked experiments and studies in patients with dengue are needed to assess the reproducibility and clinical relevance of the findings. Until such studies are conducted, the reported differences in galectin-3, galectin-9, and the seven other mediators remain an ex vivo observation rather than an explanation of clinical outcomes in older adults with dengue.
